mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted, {وَالَّذِي أنزل إِلَيْك}: الذي is in the position of nominative by conjunction to آيات, or on the implication of هو; and الحق is a naʿt (adjective) of الذي. It is also permissible for الذي to be in the position of genitive by conjunction to الكتاب, in which case الحق is nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {سَوَاء مِنْكُم من أسر}: من is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and سواء is a fronted khabar (predicate); the implied form is "of equal [standing] among you is he who conceals (ذُو سَوَاء مِنْكُم من أسر)". It is also permissible for سواء to mean "equal (مستو)", so there is no need to assume the omission of ذو.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {خوفًا وَطَمَعًا}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying {زبد مثله}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Kisāʾī said زبد is a mubtadaʾ, مثله is its naʿt (adjective), and the khabar is ومما يوقدون together with the clause. It has also been said the khabar of زبد is His saying في النار.
His saying {جفَاء}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in فيذهب, which is the pronoun of the foam (الزبد).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying {بِغَيْر عمد ترونها}: it is permissible for ترونها to be in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of عمد, the meaning being that there are pillars there but they are not seen. It is permissible for ترونها to have no grammatical position, [meaning] "and you see them [so]", so again there would be no pillars there. It is also permissible for it to be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السموات, the meaning being that there are no pillars there at all.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {وَمن صلح}: من is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), or in the position of nominative by conjunction to أولئك, or by conjunction to the nominative implied pronoun in يدخلونها. Conjoining to the nominative implied pronoun without emphasis is good because of the accusative pronoun that intervenes between them, which takes the place of the emphasis.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying {الَّذين آمنُوا وَعمِلُوا الصَّالِحَات}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); طوبى is a second mubtadaʾ, لهم is the khabar (predicate) of طوبى, and the clause is a khabar about الذين. It is also permissible for الذين to be in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from من, or on the implication of أعني ("I mean"). It is permissible for طوبى to be in the position of accusative on the implication of "He has assigned them blessedness (جعل لَهُم طُوبَى)", with وحسن مآب then accusative, but no one read it so.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {مثل الْجنَّة الَّتِي وعد المتقون}: مثل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted according to Sībawayh; its implied form is "and among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden", or "among what is narrated to you is the description of the Garden". Al-Farrāʾ said تجري من تحتها الأنهار is the khabar, his interpretation being the omission of مثل and its redundancy, and that the khabar is only about what مثل is annexed to, not about مثل itself; so it is disregarded (mulghā) and the khabar is about what comes after it, as though He said: "the Garden which the God-fearing were promised — rivers flow beneath it", just as one says "the description of so-and-so is dark-skinned (حلية فلَان أسمر)" on the assumption of the omission of الحلية.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {كفى بِاللَّه شَهِيدا}: شهيدا is accusative as a specification (bayān), and بالله is in the position of nominative.
His saying {وَمن عِنْده}: من is in the position of nominative by conjunction to the position of بالله, or in the position of genitive by conjunction to the wording.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {أئذا كُنَّا}: the governor of إذا is an omitted verb indicated by the meaning of the speech; its implied form is "shall we be resurrected when…? (أنبعث إِذا)". Whoever reads it in the form of a statement, its implied form is "we will not be resurrected when we have become…", because they denied the resurrection, and their denial indicates this omission. It is not permissible for كنا to govern إذا, because the people did not deny their becoming dust; they denied only the resurrection after becoming dust; so a verb must be implied that governs إذا, by which the meaning is completed. It has also been said that كنا does not govern إذا because إذا is annexed to كنا, and the muḍāf is not governed by [rather: does not govern] the muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: the text says "the muḍāf does not govern the muḍāf ilayhi"; i.e. the annexed-to clause cannot govern the word annexed to it]. Nor is it permissible for مبعوثون to govern إذا, because what comes after إنّ does not govern what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {وَلكُل قوم هاد}: هاد is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what precedes it, namely ولكل قوم, is its khabar (predicate); the lām is attached to [the notion of] stability (istiqrār) or permanence (thabāt). It is also permissible for هاد to be conjoined to منذر, so that the lām is attached to منذر or to هاد; its implied form being "you are only a warner, or a guide for every people".

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {يعلم مَا تحمل}: if you make مَا mean الذي, it is in the position of accusative by يعلم, and the hāʾ is omitted from تحمل, its implied form being تحمله. If you make مَا interrogative, it is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and تحمل is its khabar (predicate), with an omitted hāʾ assumed, and the clause is in the position of accusative by يعلم; this is far-fetched because of the omission of the hāʾ from the khabar, which is mostly permissible only in poetry. The best is for مَا to be in the position of accusative by تحمل, being interrogative.
